title: Tail-behavior & amortized-cost harness for HW matrix (A10/L4/A100/H100)
creator: Arjun Desai
description: Goal: Build and run a repeatable harness that measures tail latency behavior (p50/p95/p99), steady-state tokens/sec, and an amortized cost-per-token for realistic chat workloads across the hardware matrix (NVIDIA A10, L4, A100, H100). This ticket adds: 1) a new multi-pattern load generator (TokenWave) that mixes session lengths, prefill/stream ratios, and KV-cache hit rates; 2) regression detection logic (EWMA + bootstrap baseline) to detect +/- regressions in p95 and tokens/sec; 3) a cost model that separates prefill overhead, KV-hit credit, and streaming incremental token cost to provide a true amortized $/token for different sequence mixes. Scope excludes model architecture changes; focuses on serving/runtime behavior and reporting. Deliverables: harness code merged, baseline runs for four GPUs, regression alert rules, a Confluence runbook, and a dashboard tile in Datadog/Looker for daily drift checks.
acceptance_criteria: TokenWave harness merged to performance/benchmarking with CI job that runs matrix smoke tests
Baseline matrix report uploaded to Confluence with p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and amortized $/1k tokens for three sequence mixes (short-chat, mixed, long-context)
Regression detection thresholds implemented: EWMA with 14-day window + bootstrap CI; alerts configured when p95 increases >10% or tokens/sec drops >12% vs baseline
Dashboard tile shows per-GPU daily p95, tokens/sec, and cost trend; alerts firing in staging when thresholds hit
experiments: Experiment A: Steady-state multi-slab load (128 slab concurrency) with 70% short-chat (64 tokens), 20% mixed (256 tokens), 10% long (2048 tokens). Measure steady tokens/sec and p95 windows.
Experiment B: Prefill-heavy profile (90% long-context prefill + 10% streaming) to measure amortized prefill cost and KV cache gains over session reuse.
Experiment C: Burst + cool-down pattern to exercise tail amplification under autoscale handoffs and kernel-scheduling transitions.
Each experiment runs on A10, L4, A100, H100 with identical model binary and quantization profile to isolate hardware/runtime differences.
preliminary_findings: A10: steady tokens/sec ~11,900; p95 (steady) ~78ms; prefill-heavy runs show 14% higher amortized $/1k tokens due to slower prefill parallelism
L4: steady tokens/sec ~18,200; p95 (steady) ~62ms; shows best cost per token for mixed workloads but exhibits a 9% p95 spike during slab handovers in burst tests
A100: steady tokens/sec ~29,500; p95 (steady) ~48ms; amortized $/1k tokens competitive but exhibits larger variance on long-context prefill (p99 increases up to 2.4x baseline under contentions)
H100: steady tokens/sec ~33,800; p95 (steady) ~44ms; highest throughput and lowest steady p95 but prefill amortization benefit smaller vs A100 due to higher absolute prefill cost
KV-cache effect: enabling generous cache reuse (simulated 60% hit) reduced amortized $/1k tokens by 18-27% across HW, disproportionately benefitting A10 and L4 where prefill is relatively expensive
Regression detection baseline: initial bootstrap CI indicates current p95 stable within +/-6% for A100/H100 but L4 requires smoothing to avoid false positives during autoscale events
